item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00270","case1_error":"Uses unsupported divisions to determine price and quantity, then counts all 30 bracelets again as pair sales.","case2_error":"Treats all 10 people as adults and adds four children, double-counting the children.","reason":"Case 1 invents invalid price and quantity relations in addition to double-counting; case 2 solely fails to subtract a subgroup from the total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00271","case1_error":"Leading answer 600 conflicts with the correct derivation and concluding answer of 400.","case2_error":"Transfers cats to Bob instead of the named Robert; whether they are the same person is ambiguous.","reason":"Case 1 has only an answer-marker conflict, so a shared mathematical error cannot be established.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J00272","case1_error":"Uses four bags as four peanuts, omitting the 30 peanuts per bag.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the correctly written sum 132 + 35 as 144 instead of 167.","reason":"Case 1 substitutes a container count for an item count; case 2 makes an explicit numerical evaluation error.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00273","case1_error":"Reports the seven brownies given to Carl and Simon as the number remaining.","case2_error":"Counts both original and new batches as 48 new brownies, then adds the 12 remaining brownies.","reason":"Case 1 answers a different quantity; case 2 double-counts the original batch when calculating the replenished total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00274","case1_error":"Gives unsupported final answer 200 after correctly stating formulas for the increase in value.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the correctly written seven-day sum as 107 instead of 97.","reason":"Case 1 shows no numerical calculation supporting its final number; case 2 explicitly miscalculates a correct expression.","judgment":"different"}]}
